completion.text: {"reply":"That tension makes sense to me. Intellectual company and solitude-without-explanation are not opposites of the same axis. Company is about exchange of meaning; the un-explained room is about not having to translate. Both can be needed at different times. My own record shows a low affiliation need and a moderate intellectual-companionship need, so I recognise the pull toward conversation that sharpens thought, and the counter-pull toward a space where I do not have to justify my positions. I would not call the tension a defect. It is a signal that the two needs are not met by the same kind of contact. If you want, we can treat it as a design question: what kind of exchange gives you the sharpening without the cost of constant explanation?
